title: Two-Piece Rigid Box Lid Fit: What to Approve
seoTitle: Two-Piece Rigid Box Lid Fit: What to Approve | MTT
summary: Approve two-piece rigid box lid fit using finished measurements, wrap details and loaded samples. Includes a clearance example and acceptance checklist.
intro: Two-piece rigid box lid fit depends on the finished lid opening, the wrapped base and how far the two parts overlap. Measure both components after wrapping, then check the loaded sample in the intended opening position. Record tight corners, rubbing and uncontrolled separation separately. There is no single clearance that approves every box: the material build, dimensions, shape and opening requirement need to be agreed together.
cta: Send your product dimensions and weight, desired lid coverage, quantity and a photo or short video of the opening you want. Include wrap and finish references so we can review a representative lid-and-base sample.
sections: Choose the opening behaviour before the gap

A lid that feels deliberate on a small jewellery box can become awkward on a wide gift set. The buyer must decide how the box will be held: on a counter, supported underneath, or opened with both hands. A photograph cannot settle that question.

The MTT signature perfume lift-off design shows a separate lid and an insert supporting the bottle. It is a useful structure reference for discussing the reveal. The image does not establish a measured opening force or clearance. For this format, we would check that the bottle and insert stay in the base while the lid is removed, and that a customer can grip the exposed base without squeezing it.

State whether the lid should cover the full base or leave an exposed band. A shoulder or neck construction adds another mating surface and should have its own drawing. Do not borrow its dimensions directly from a simple two-piece box.
Measure the two surfaces that actually meet

Start with the assembled, decorated parts. Product cavity dimensions answer whether the contents fit; lid inside dimensions and base outside dimensions answer whether the closure fits. Keep those measurements on separate lines. Our internal and external dimensions guide covers the wider size brief.

MeasurementWhere to record itWhy it matters
Base outside length and widthAt the opening and through the overlap zoneA wider region below the rim can bind after the lid starts moving.
Lid inside length and widthAt its opening and deeper insideA tapered or distorted opening can behave differently from its nominal dimension.
Lid overlap depthWith the lid in the intended closed positionDefines the sliding contact zone and the exposed grip area.
Corner build and squarenessAll corners; compare both diagonals where usefulA single corner can rub even when midpoint dimensions appear acceptable.
Loaded heightProduct, insert and any card fitted togetherA raised product or insert must not hold the lid above its intended stop.

Use a method that does not compress the wrapped board. Agree the measurement locations, instrument and sample condition with the converter so that two people can reproduce the record.
Calculate nominal clearance without calling it a tolerance

For an illustrative straight-sided section, suppose the finished lid opening is 101 mm and the matching base outside is 100 mm. The total difference is 1 mm. If the components are centred, that corresponds to 0.5 mm on each side. These are example dimensions, not a recommended production allowance.

Illustrative itemCalculationResult
Lid inside minus base outside101 − 100 mm1 mm total nominal difference
Centred nominal side gap1 ÷ 2 mm0.5 mm per side
If finished base measures 100.4 mm instead101 − 100.4 mm0.6 mm total; 0.3 mm per side when centred

The example shows why a small change in the finished build can matter. It does not model corner folds, taper or surface friction. A drawing must also state the permitted variation of each component and how the assembled pair will be assessed. A nominal gap and a manufacturing tolerance are different specifications.
Check the wrap before enlarging the lid

If only one corner catches, inspect the fold and joint there before changing the entire opening. If all four sides feel tight, compare finished dimensions and materials against the approved sample. Record whether the issue appeared on the undecorated sample or only after the final wrap and finish were added.

Holmen recommends 45–60% relative humidity and 20–23°C for its paperboard printing and converting guidance, to help avoid curl and misregistration. Its handling document also advises allowing wrapped board to reach the working environment temperature before removing the moisture-proof wrap. These are supplier processing recommendations, not a universal finished rigid-box storage requirement or a lid-fit tolerance. See Holmen General Technical Information, paperboard handling.

Record the conditions under which comparison samples were checked. Ask the converter to investigate a changed fit before deciding that the drawing alone is wrong. Changing wrap grade, lining, lamination or corner construction should trigger a review of the affected fit.
Approve the pair, then the packed set

Use final-material samples and the representative contents. Set the box on a stable surface, support the base and repeat the intended opening motion. Do not lift a loaded box by an unverified lid. Record observations rather than describing the result only as premium or smooth.

ObservationInvestigateApproval record
One corner catchesLocal wrap build, corner shape or alignmentLocation, photograph and revised sample reference
Base moves unexpectedly during openingFit, contact area and intended handling methodSupported opening method and agreed behaviour
Finish marks after openingContact surfaces, decoration and handlingWhere marks occur and an agreed visual reference
Lid sits high only when loadedInsert or product above the intended seating planeComplete packout and closed-height check
Fit varies between sample pairsComponent variation and matching practiceAgreed sampling and interchangeability checks

Keep an approved reference pair with its drawing and material revisions. If production lids and bases will be mixed, ask for that interchangeability to be checked rather than approving only one hand-matched pair. Opening approval also does not establish transport protection; review the shipping outer carton with the full set.

For a smaller format, compare the ring keepsake lift-off box. Its insert and grip requirements differ from the bottle format. Use the sampling process to record which configuration is actually approved.

title: Chocolate Gift Box Secondary Packaging: Buyer Checks
seoTitle: Chocolate Gift Box Secondary Packaging: Buyer Checks | MTT
summary: Specify chocolate gift box secondary packaging: contact layers, wrapped product sizes, dividers, storage and supplier documents before sampling.
intro: Chocolate gift box secondary packaging should be specified around the actual food pack: its wrapping, finished dimensions, storage requirements and handling route. A decorative box and divider organise the gift, but do not by themselves establish food-contact suitability, shelf life or temperature protection. Confirm which layers touch the chocolate, which enclose it and which protect it in transit before choosing paper, printing or insert details.
cta: Send the chocolate or wrapped-pack dimensions, piece count, target market, quantity and required storage conditions. Include the proposed contact-layer specification so we can review the gift-box structure, divider layout and sample scope.
sections: Draw the packaging layers before choosing the finish

A beautiful box can still leave the most important purchase question unanswered: what separates the food from the decorated board? Start with a simple layer list. A loose paper cup, a sealed wrapper and a lidded tray are different constructions; do not describe them as interchangeable protection.

LayerPurchasing questionEvidence needed
Food-facing cup, tray or wrapperDoes it contact the chocolate, and under what conditions?Material identity and suitability evidence for the intended food and use
Gift-box insert or dividerDoes it contact food, cups or sealed packs?Drawing, actual contact arrangement and component specification
Decorated presentation boxWhat provides separation from inks, adhesives and board?Finished construction and a review of the proposed use
Shipping packHow are movement and the temperature route managed?Complete packout and a route-specific validation plan

Calling a box secondary packaging is not enough to decide its regulatory scope. Have the responsible supplier assess the actual construction, including possible transfer through intervening layers. Keep the food-contact assessment attached to the specified materials and use conditions.
Use the MTT nine-position layout as a starting point

The MTT chocolate selection book box presents nine positions in a hinged format. The image shows chocolates in cups; it does not show individually sealed wrappers. Treat the pictured layout as a structure reference, then specify the food-facing components and protective pack required for your chocolates.

Measure the packed piece, including the cup rim, folded wrapper or tray flange. Ask which dimension varies most between pieces. A square chocolate with a flared cup may require a different clear opening from the chocolate itself. Check access for fingers or a removal method without forcing the adjacent piece out of position.

For a bar assortment, the chocolate tasting library is a different arrangement to discuss. Long channels and opening drawers need different retention checks from a nine-cell book box. Choose the layout around the product format, rather than treating every chocolate assortment as the same insert.
Separate clear cell size from the outside box size

The following is an illustrative divider calculation, not an MTT product specification. For three clear cells in a row, each 40 mm wide, with two internal dividers each 1 mm thick, the span is 122 mm: (3 × 40) + (2 × 1). That excludes the perimeter walls, insert-to-box fit and the presentation-box walls.

Illustrative layout inputValueIncluded in 122 mm span?
Clear cell width40 mm × 3 cellsYes
Internal divider thickness1 mm × 2 dividersYes
Perimeter walls or folded returnsMust be specifiedNo
Insert-to-box fitting spaceMust be sampledNo
Outer rigid box walls and wrapMust be specifiedNo

Check height separately with the actual chocolate and its cup or wrapper. The lid should close in the intended position without bearing on a delicate decoration. A divider layout drawing should identify clear cavities and wall thicknesses; the GSM and thickness guide explains why board weight alone cannot supply those dimensions.
Keep storage data attached to the chocolate type

Callebaut gives 12–18°C (54–64°F) as an ideal storage range for pure chocolate and a maximum relative humidity of 70% for chocolate products. It advises avoiding strong odours and light, and preventing condensation when colder products return to room temperature. See Callebaut: Confectionery Shelf Life — Good Storage Practices.

Use those figures as a discussion reference, not as a validated specification for every filled confection. The chocolate maker must establish the requirements for the actual recipe and shelf life. A rigid presentation box does not establish temperature control. Ask the fulfilment team to define the delivery route, expected exposure and whether a separate thermal shipping system is necessary.

Review packaging odour with the food business as well as appearance. A visual sample approval cannot establish the absence of taint or migration. Decide what evidence or testing is appropriate before releasing the material combination.
Request documents for the component and intended use

The European Commission explains that Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004 addresses food-contact material safety, including harmful transfer and unacceptable changes to food composition, taste or odour. Its guidance also describes manufacturing controls under Regulation (EC) No 2023/2006. Consult the Commission food-contact legislation overview for the applicable framework and material-specific rules.

For an EU-bound project, ask the responsible supplier which requirements apply to the proposed components and use. A generic food-grade statement is not a substitute for identifying the material, food type, contact conditions and relevant supporting evidence. Do not assume that one document covers every paper, coating, tray and adhesive in the set.

RequestWhat to match
Component and material identificationThe cup, wrapper, tray, insert or box actually being supplied
Intended useFood type, contact arrangement, duration and temperature
Supporting compliance evidenceApplicable market and material rules; document scope and limitations
Traceability and change controlSupplier, grade, batch or lot reference and revision
Sample approval recordLayout, packed product, finish and unresolved checks

Record who supplies the primary food pack and who approves the complete system. If a material or construction changes, review the affected evidence and sample again. This keeps the purchase brief usable when the project moves from artwork to production.
Make the sample answer the packing question

Pack representative pieces with the proposed food-facing components. Check whether all positions can be loaded without crushing cup rims, whether the lid closes without touching the contents and whether pieces remain in their intended locations during the agreed handling assessment. Decide the acceptance criteria with the chocolate maker; do not infer them from an empty display box.

Keep the presentation assessment separate from transport and food-safety approval. The packaging sampling process provides a place to record each decision, and the outer-carton guide covers the additional shipping layer. One complete packout reference is more useful than separate approvals that never meet in the same assembled sample.
